title: Substitute
text: Let $$x=2sin\left(\theta\right)$$. Then the integral becomes $$\frac{1}{4}$$ times the integral of $${\operatorname{csc}\left(\theta\right)}^2$$ with respect to θ, which is $$-\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) \operatorname{cot}\left(\theta\right)$$.

title: Evaluate
text: In terms of $$x$$, the antiderivative is $$\frac{-\sqrt{4-x^2}}{4x}$$. At $$x=2$$ it is $$0$$, and at $$x=1$$ it is $$\frac{-\sqrt{3}}{4}$$.
